scenes.headline: How Jev answers, and why it moves
scenes.sub: One pass, one option, two kinds of drift.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Elder! Jev picks one of the options you send. Here's how, and two separate reasons its answer moves.

scenes.text: Jev reads its answer off one forward pass, so nothing is sampled. Yet resending a question moves it, and reordering the options moves it more.
scenes.mark: reordering the options moves it more
scenes.say: Jev samples nothing. Yet resending a question moves its answer; reordering the options moves it more.

scenes.title: One request, one probability per option

steps.say: You send a question, its evidence, and a menu of options: seventy-seven, in this benchmark.
Jev scores them in one forward pass. No seed, no temperature: nothing is drawn token by token.
Out comes a probability for every option, rounded to two decimals.

steps.note: No hallucination is a closure property, not a promise of correctness
steps.say: The answer is always one you sent. That's the no-hallucination claim: closure, not correctness.

scenes.title: Two ways to read out a choice

left.title: A letter readout
items: Options go in as lettered text
A, B and C carry different priors
left.say: A letter readout picks a token. On one open model, slot A alone was worth about one point seven logits.

right.title: A per-option scorer
items: Each option scored alone, against the context
Shuffling options only shuffles the output rows
Order effect: exactly zero, by construction
right.say: A per-option scorer rates each option alone. Shuffle the menu and only the rows shuffle: no order effect.

items.say: Not sampling: there's nothing to sample.
Not the version: every response named one pinned model.
Not the client: identical input tokens, every time.
What's left is serving: batches, kernels, the fleet. Reasoned guess: if Jev is a mixture of experts, routing depends on the batch.

steps.say: That open project's scorer on a Mac: same fixture and pinned checkpoint as its published CUDA run.
Every winner agrees. Scores move by up to point one oh five: an eighth of what reversing the options buys.

scenes.label: The published 13%, split apart
scenes.note: 4 items did both; the union is the published 13
scenes.say: The published thirteen percent pools both. Split: twelve items flip with the order, five with nothing changed, four with both.

scenes.text: The answer is always one you offered, but it isn't a property of the question alone. Average a few orderings before thresholding.
scenes.mark: a property of the question alone
scenes.say: The answer is always one you offered, but not a property of the question alone. Average a few orderings before thresholding.

recap: One forward pass: a probability for every option
Resending moves it; reordering moves it more
scenes.say: To recap: one pass, two kinds of drift, one published number holding both.
